title: Formation of the Sahara desert
summary: During the Tortonian stage of the Late Miocene, about seven to eleven million years ago, the shrinkage of the ancient Tethys Sea weakened the African summer monsoon. This triggered progressive aridification across North Africa, initiating the formation of the modern Sahara desert. The transition created the largest hot desert on Earth, profoundly altering regional atmospheric circulation and continental ecosystems.

uncertainty.note: Climate modeling dates the primary Tortonian aridification trigger to approximately 7 to 11 million years ago (Zhang et al. 2014); eolian sand dune deposits in northern Chad confirm desert conditions by approximately 7 Ma (Schuster et al. 2006).

where.historical_name: Northern Africa, Late Miocene; no polities existed
